1 Introduction

1.1 Project Overview

This report replicates in R the Cricket Score Prediction project originally developed in Python for the ML2 – Machine Learning 2 course (Rajat Dogra & Umair Aziz, January 2026).

Objective: Predict IPL cricket match scores (continuous target) using ball-by-ball match data from the IPL Dataset 2008–2025.

Research question: Can match contextual features (run rate, wickets, venue, team, toss) reliably predict cricket scores using regression models?

1.2 Dataset

  • Source: IPL Dataset 2008–2025
  • Size: 76,014 ball-by-ball records, 60+ features
  • Target: final_score — the total runs scored in an innings

2.2 Feature Correlations

Show code 
numeric_cols <- df %>% select(where(is.numeric))

correlations <- numeric_cols %>%
  summarise(across(everything(),
                   ~cor(., df$final_score, use = "complete.obs"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to  = "feature",
               values_to = "correlation") %>%
  filter(feature != "final_score") %>%
  mutate(abs_corr = abs(correlation)) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs_corr)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)

kable(correlations,
      caption = "Top 5 Features Correlated with final_score",
      digits  = 3)

3 Data Preprocessing & Feature Engineering

Show code 
# Select features matching Python pipeline
selected_features <- c(
  "innings", "team", "wickets_lost", "balls_faced",
  "venue", "city", "toss_winner", "toss_decision",
  "year", "month", "day", "target_score"
)

# Keep only columns that exist
selected_features <- selected_features[selected_features %in% names(df)]

df_model <- df %>%
  select(all_of(selected_features), final_score) %>%
  drop_na()

cat("Features selected:", length(selected_features), "\n")
Features selected: 12
Show code 
cat("Rows after dropping NAs:", nrow(df_model), "\n")
Rows after dropping NAs: 1164

3.2 Preprocessing Recipe

Show code 
rec <- recipe(final_score ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_other(all_nominal_predictors(), threshold = 0.01) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

4 Baseline Model Training

Show code 
baseline_results <- read_csv(
  here("regression", "output", "baseline_ranking.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE

Six baseline models were trained using 5-fold cross-validation, replicating the Python pipeline.

Baseline Model Rankings — Test Set Performance
Rank Model MAE RMSE R²
1 Random Forest 15.480 20.690 0.702

3 XGBoost 15.480 21.209 0.680
4 Neural Network 17.605 23.035 0.627
5 Linear Regression 18.063 23.082 0.617

Key finding: Random Forest achieves R²=0.702 as the best baseline model, compared to the Python baseline of R²=0.6989. ✅

5.3 Comparison with Python Baseline

Show code 
best_r2   <- max(final_results$R2)
best_model <- final_results$Model[which.max(final_results$R2)]
best_rmse  <- final_results$RMSE[which.max(final_results$R2)]
best_mae   <- final_results$MAE[which.max(final_results$R2)]

comparison <- tibble(
  Metric  = c("Best Model", "R²", "RMSE", "MAE"),
  R_Result = c(best_model,
               sprintf("%.3f", best_r2),
               sprintf("%.1f", best_rmse),
               sprintf("%.1f", best_mae)),
  Python_Baseline = c("Gradient Boosting Optimised",
                      "0.722", "20.1", "14.8")
)

kable(comparison,
      caption = "R Replication vs Python Baseline",
      col.names = c("Metric", "R Result", "Python Baseline"))
R Replication vs Python Baseline

7 Summary & Conclusions

7.1 Key Findings

  • Best model: Voting Ensemble (Stack) with R²=0.749, RMSE=19.2 runs, MAE=13.8 runs
  • Python baseline beaten: R²=0.749 vs Python 0.722 ✅
  • Hyperparameter tuning improved XGBoost R² by 0.064 and Random Forest by 0.021
  • Key predictors: target_score and balls_faced most correlated with final score

7.2 Practical Applications

  • Sports analytics: Team strategy optimisation
  • Broadcasting: Real-time score predictions
  • Fantasy sports: Player valuation
  • Coaching: Tactical decision support

7.3 Reproducibility Notes

  • All packages pinned via renv.lock
  • Random seed set to 42 throughout
  • No absolute paths — here() package used throughout
  • Pipeline runs end-to-end with three source() commands:
    1. source("regression/cricket_score_prediction.R")
    2. source("regression/03_baseline_models.R")
    3. source("regression/04_tuning_ensembles.R")
